# ROOTS-AI™ — vendor copy register (outside the report)

Every string a participant reads that **no controlled pack supplies**, listed for ROOTS
approval. Prepared in response to the ROOTS review of 29 September 2026, item D7, which
found this wording described as "marked PENDING and listed for approval" against a register
that did not exist.

**Generated by** `npm run check:vendor-copy`, from the copy module itself, so the register
cannot drift from what the product says. Each string is checked against the controlled C-04
pack: a string that turns out to be *in* C-04 fails the run, because copy we treat as ours
being approved after all means it should be read from the governed module instead.

The report's own wording is not here. It is registered separately, against C-03 and the
issued review, by `npm run check:c03`.

## Summary

| | Strings |
|---|---|
| Vendor-drafted, awaiting approval | **70** |
| — of which **assert a behaviour** (governed; section 1) | **20** |
| — of which are neutral interface copy (section 2) | 50 |
| — of which reuse wording from inside an approved sentence | 1 |
| Standalone in C-04 after all (a defect, fails the run) | 0 |

A button reading *"Request a new secure link"* is not approved copy merely because those
words occur inside C-04's approved sentence *"...this session has expired. Request a new
secure link to continue."* The first is a label we wrote; the second is a message the pack
supplies. Strings in that position are marked **(reuses approved wording)** below and listed
for approval like any other, because claiming otherwise would claim an approval we do not
hold. They are worth ROOTS' attention first: the wording is already ROOTS', so approving it
should be quick.

## What this wording is, and is not

It is functional: field labels, button text, progress indicators, error messages and the
sentences that explain what a control does. C-04 governs the website and legal copy and the
approved consent and system messages; it does not supply a label for every input or a message
for every failure, and a screen cannot be built without them.

Every string here is written to the same constraints: minimal, neutral, no claim, no promise,
and no health statement. None of them states a finding, a score, a classification or anything
about a participant's biology — that wording is all governed and is all in the C-03 register.

**What approval would settle.** Each string accepted as written, amended, or replaced with
approved wording. Where ROOTS amends one, it is replaced verbatim and this register
regenerates.

## 1. Behaviour-asserting copy — governed, source-bound

ROOTS review of 30 September 2026, section 5. Acceptance of ordinary functional copy
**does not extend** to consent, privacy, data retention/deletion/export,
authentication/security behaviour, age acknowledgement, medical boundaries, AI disclosure,
immutable/final records, or offline data behaviour. ROOTS further required that claims such
as data being archived, retained on-device while offline, use of email, final-record
behaviour and consent effects be *"supported by the implemented behavior and governing
specification, not merely categorized as ‘functional copy’"*.

The test applied is not whether a string mentions a topic. *"Email address"* is a field label
and asserts nothing. The test is whether the string makes a claim a participant could rely
on. Each one below is listed with the claim it makes and what supports it; the run fails if
any governed string has no recorded support.

### `emailPrivacyNote` — Privacy; use of email

> We use your email only to send your secure link. See the Privacy Notice.

**Claim.** The address is used only to send the secure link.

**What supports it.** `app/api/v1/auth/magic-link/route.ts` uses the address to provision the account and generate the link, and for a rate-limit digest; it is stored on the profile and used for no other purpose. Contact enquiries go to a separate configured address. No marketing or analytics use exists. Governed by the Privacy Notice (C-04).

*Screen: ASM-01 secure link.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `ageAcknowledgement` — Age acknowledgement

> I confirm that I am 18 or older.

**Claim.** The participant confirms they are 18 or older.

**What supports it.** C-01 VAL-010 and `MIN_ELIGIBLE_AGE = 18`. The magic-link route requires `ageConfirmed: true` and refuses the request without it; Q1 below 18 is refused by `validateAnswer` with the approved VAL-010 wording.

*Screen: ASM-01 secure link.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `checkEmailBody` — Authentication behaviour

> If the address can be used, we have sent a secure link to it. The link works once and expires after a short time. Check your inbox and spam folder.

**Claim.** The response is the same whether or not the address is registered; the link works once and expires.

**What supports it.** The route returns an identical body either way — asserted by `tests/auth/provisioning.test.ts`, *account existence is never revealed*. Single use and expiry are Supabase Auth one-time tokens with `MAGIC_LINK_EXPIRY_MINUTES` (15).

*Screen: ASM-01 secure link.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `linkErrorBody` — Authentication behaviour

> Secure links work once and expire after a short time. Request a new link to continue.

**Claim.** Secure links work once and expire after a short time.

**What supports it.** As above. `app/auth/confirm/route.ts` verifies the one-time token and redirects to the error screen when it is used or expired.

*Screen: ASM-01 link error.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `signedInAs` — Authentication behaviour

> Signed in as {email}

**Claim.** Names the signed-in account.

**What supports it.** Rendered from the verified Supabase session (`getParticipant`), not from an unvalidated cookie.

*Screen: ASM-02 consent.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `consentRequired` — Consent

> Please agree to continue.

**Claim.** Agreement is required to continue.

**What supports it.** The consent screen blocks progression until the required consent is recorded in `consents`; `POST /api/v1/consents` is the only writer.

*Screen: ASM-02 consent.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `consentSaveFailed` — Consent

> We could not save your choice. Please try again.

**Claim.** The choice was not saved and should be retried.

**What supports it.** Shown only on a failed `POST /api/v1/consents`. No consent is treated as given on failure.

*Screen: ASM-02 consent.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `consentVersion` — Consent

> Version {version} • Effective {date}

**Claim.** States the consent document version and effective date.

**What supports it.** Filled from `LEGAL_VERSION`, and the same version is stored on the `consents` row, so what was shown and what was recorded cannot differ.

*Screen: ASM-02 consent.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `savePrivacy` — Data behaviour; authentication

> Your answers save automatically as you go. To return later, request a new secure link with the same email.

**Claim.** Answers save automatically; returning requires a new secure link to the same address.

**What supports it.** Autosave is `PATCH /api/v1/assessments/[id]/responses`, called per answer. Resume requires a verified session, and a session is only obtained through a secure link; an assessment is bound to its profile by `assessments.profile_id` and RLS refuses any other.

*Screen: ASM-03 start.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `saveExitBody` — Data retention; authentication

> Your saved answers stay with your assessment. To continue later, request a new secure link using the same email.

**Claim.** Saved answers stay with the assessment; continuing requires a new secure link to the same address.

**What supports it.** As above. Nothing is discarded on exit: `responses` rows persist and the assessment stays `in_progress`.

*Screen: ASM-05 save and exit.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `restartConfirmBody` — Immutable records; data retention

> Your saved answers for this assessment will be archived and a new, empty assessment will start. This cannot be undone.

**Claim.** The existing answers are **archived**, a new empty assessment starts, and this cannot be undone.

**What supports it.** `app/api/v1/assessments/[id]/archive/route.ts` sets `status = 'archived'` and `archived_at`. **Nothing is deleted** — the answers remain in `responses` and are included in a data export. The claim is 'archived', not 'deleted', and that is what the code does. Irreversibility: no endpoint un-archives an assessment.

*Screen: ASM-06 resume.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `reportNameSaveFailed` — Data behaviour

> We could not save your name. Try again, or clear the field to continue.

**Claim.** The name was not saved and the field may be cleared to continue.

**What supports it.** `PATCH /api/v1/profile`; the column privilege limits the write to `display_name`. The report renders the approved fallback when it is blank.

*Screen: ASM-07 review.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `reviewBoundary` — Immutable / final records

> When you submit, your answers are saved as a final record and can no longer be changed. Your answers generate educational wellness indicators, not a diagnosis.

**Claim.** On submission the answers become a final record and can no longer be changed.

**What supports it.** `app/api/v1/assessments/[id]/responses/route.ts` refuses any write once `status !== 'in_progress'`, returning 409 `ASSESSMENT_CLOSED`. Submission sets the status, so the record is closed by the same transition the sentence describes.

*Screen: ASM-07 review.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `submitFailed` — Data behaviour

> We could not submit your assessment. Your answers are saved. Please try again.

**Claim.** The submission failed but the answers are saved.

**What supports it.** Autosave has already persisted each answer before submit is called, so the statement holds: a failed submit leaves `responses` intact and the assessment `in_progress`.

*Screen: ASM-08 submitted.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `signOut` — Authentication behaviour

> Sign out

**Claim.** Ends the session.

**What supports it.** `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-out` clears the Supabase session cookies.

*Screen: Assessment, shared.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `offline` — Offline data behaviour

> You are offline. Your current entry remains on this device until you leave or refresh.

**Claim.** The current entry remains on this device until the participant leaves or refreshes.

**What supports it.** The in-progress answer is React component state only. There is no `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` or IndexedDB persistence of answers anywhere in `app/assessment/` or `lib/assessment/`, so it is lost on leave or refresh exactly as stated. **Disclosure:** `sessionStorage` is used for two non-answer values — the email typed at entry, and a submit idempotency key — and those do survive a refresh within the tab. Neither is an answer, and neither is what this sentence describes, but ROOTS should know they exist.

*Screen: Assessment, shared.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `extendSession` — Authentication behaviour

> Stay signed in

**Claim.** The session can be kept alive.

**What supports it.** `proxy.ts` refreshes and rotates the Supabase session on each protected request; idle timeout is `ASSESSMENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`.

*Screen: Assessment, shared.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `magicLinkSubject` — Authentication behaviour; use of email

> Your ROOTS-AI™ secure link

**Claim.** Identifies the email as carrying a secure link.

**What supports it.** `lib/email/mailer.ts`; the only participant email the system sends.

*Screen: Secure-link email.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `magicLinkEmailBody` — Authentication behaviour

> Use this secure link to continue to your ROOTS Biological Assessment. It works once and expires in {minutes} minutes. {link} If you did not request this link, you can ignore this email.

**Claim.** The link works once and expires after the stated number of minutes.

**What supports it.** The minutes value is filled from `MAGIC_LINK_EXPIRY_MINUTES`, the same setting Supabase enforces, so the stated figure cannot drift from the configured one.

*Screen: Secure-link email.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

### `requestNewLink` — Authentication behaviour

> Request a new secure link

**Claim.** A new link can be requested.

**What supports it.** Reuses wording from inside C-04's approved session-expiry sentence. Rate limited to `MAGIC_LINK_MAX_REQUESTS` (3) per 15 minutes.

*Screen: ASM-01 link error.* **ROOTS decision:** ______

## Placeholders

`{name}` marks a value filled at render time — a count, a module title, a timestamp, an email
address. The surrounding words are the wording being approved; the placeholder is not.
